articles.title: East of Eden Review
articles.summary: Beautifully shot and dramatically riveting, Netflix's East of Eden, starring Florence Pugh, Christopher Abbott and Mike Faist, is definitely binge-worthy TV.
body: Good vs. evil, brotherly rivalries, parental rejection, the notion of free will as opposed to fate… East of Eden has a lot going on. And the new Netflix iteration of the John Steinbeck epic is pretty great at conveying these ideas with a well-acted, handsomely produced, seven-episode miniseries that’s the streaming equivalent of a page-turner.

I confess to having never seen Elia Kazan’s 1955 adaptation of East of Eden in its entirety, despite its status as one of only three starring vehicles for James Dean. But what I do remember about it is mish-mashed in my head with another of his films, Giant, so much so that I was a bit surprised by how this version ended. That may also be in part because, surprisingly, there haven’t been a ton of film or TV adaptations of East of Eden beyond the Kazan/Dean film; there was a TV miniseries in 1981 starring Jane Seymour, and a long-gestating movie version that had Jennifer Lawrence attached at one point but never materialized, but otherwise that’s it.

articles.title: A Fan-Favorite League of Legends Champion Is Finally Joining Riftbound
articles.summary: One of the more interesting aspects of League of Legends is that gameplay in the multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) is a bit like soccer. Some players pick a lane and attack, while others hang back and play defense.
body: Graves is a mercenary, gambler, and wanted criminal who carries an enormous double-barreled shotgun named Destiny. He’s also an S-tier “jungler,” according to data from Mobalytics, which was updated following Sept. 22’s patch. That makes him one of the very best Champions in the game, especially when it comes to climbing the ranks below Diamond.

Despite that prominence and popularity, Graves hasn’t ever appeared in Riftbound, Riot Games’ physical trading card game… until now. Polygon can exclusively reveal Graves, Blasting Through, a new card coming in Riftbound ’s upcoming Radiance set, which has a global release date of Oct. 23.

Graves, Blasting Through is a rare Champion Unit that costs 5 Energy and one Fury (Red) Rune to play. He enters with 4 Might and an ability that activates whenever he attacks or defends: Graves deals damage equal to his Might to every enemy unit at that battlefield, but does not deal conventional combat damage.

articles.title: As Xbox swings the axe, Gears of War: E-Day developers fear they'll be laid off straight after launch - and right before they'd be due their bonuses
articles.summary: Back in July, new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced a total of 3,200 job cuts across Microsoft's gaming arm, with roughly half of those cuts being made alongside that announcement. The impact was vast.
body: But there's been one Xbox-owned studio left largely off the cutting block so far: Gears of War: E-Day developer The Coalition. Now, following the latest wave of Microsoft cuts - including the sudden departure of E-Day's story director, Juan Vaca - Eurogamer has learned staff at the studio have become increasingly fearful of imminent layoffs, and the potentially major financial consequences which could follow. Eurogamer spoke to multiple sources at the Vancouver-based studio with knowledge of the situation for this article, who have been provided anonymity to protect their identity.

It's worth noting that this sense of trepidation wasn't always the case. Before the latest round of Xbox layoffs, developers at The Coalition had been cautiously optimistic. They believed The Coalition had been spared the cuts, at least thus far, for two main reasons: first, they were working on a big, imminent release for Xbox, in the upcoming Gears of War: E-Day - laying off developers still working on a game would make little sense.

articles.title: KPop Demon Hunters 2 Just Changed Netflix Movie Releases Forever
articles.summary: When KPop Demon Hunters made Netflix history as its most-watched original title, a longing among fans only intensified: what would it be like to watch KPop Demon Hunters in theaters? Netflix responded by giving fans exactly what they wanted with a limited theatrical release on Aug. 23 and 24, 2025.
body: It was a risky move for Netflix, but KPop Demon Hunters ' success in theaters clearly exceeded expectations, and it appears it could also have an impact on Netflix's policy in the future. On Sept. 30, Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos revealed at Bloomberg Screentime in Los Angeles that KPop Demon Hunters 2 will have a very different release than the original.
"When the KPop Demon Hunters sequel comes, you can expect a very broad theatrical release," Sarandos said.

This is a major shake-up for Netflix, best known for releasing TV shows and films to be watched from the comfort of people's homes. However, KPop Demon Hunters 2 won't be the first Netflix movie to get a full 45-day run on the silver screen; that honor goes to the Spanish film La Bola Negra. Greta Gerwig's Narnia will also appear in theaters, along with the exciting animated adaptation of Charlie vs. The Chocolate Factory.

Meanwhile, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, written by Quentin Tarantino, directed by David Fincher, and starring Brad Pitt, will be the first Netflix to get an IMAX release, coming this November.

articles.title: LEGO PlayStation Is Now Available for LEGO Insiders
articles.summary: Good news, retro gaming fans: the LEGO set based on the original PlayStation console is now available ( see it at LEGO ). The only catch is that you need to be a LEGO Insider to buy it. Thankfully, you can sign up for free right here.
body: LEGO PlayStation is a near 1:1 scale set of Sony’s original gaming console, which came out in 1994 in Japan and 1995 in the US. It includes the console as well as the original no-analog-sticks PlayStation controller (the DualShock wouldn’t arrive until three years later).

As with most pricy LEGO sets for adults, the LEGO PS1 has some fun Easter eggs to find. First of all, set's box calls back to the box the original PlayStation came in, which is pretty great. The set's Power and Open buttons actually work. Pressing Power flips a green LEGO piece into view underneath it, as if you were turning it on. The Open button releases the disc cover, letting you see two dioramas hidden inside.

The dioramas are based on Gran Turismo (1997) and Ape Escape (1999). These dioramas can also be removed from the set to display on their own (though that leaves a hole on either side of the PS1 model).
As for LEGO Astro Bot, it's a free Gift With Purchase, but you'll be able to buy it separately at PlayStation Direct for $24.99.

The only catch is that you need to be a LEGO Insider to buy it.

articles.title: The Division studio Massive expands to take control of Splinter Cell and Ghost Recon, and a new IP, in Ubisoft's most recent reorganisation
articles.summary: Ubisoft has expanded the remit of Swedish studio Massive Entertainment - responsible for The Division series, Star Wars Outlaws and Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora - to become a second major part of the company and include more of its studios and game brands.
body: Ubisoft's Creative House 2 cluster of studios now joins the expanded Massive Entertainment brand, the company announced this week, which means Massive Entertainment now governs the Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon and Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell brands, and multiple studios around the world.

"The Massive Entertainment brand builds on a nearly three-decade legacy established in Sweden through its games and technology, earning the trust of players and recognition from industry peers alike," Massive said in a press release.

Christoph Hartmann, who was appointed as general manager of Ubisoft Creative House 2 earlier this year, has become general manager of Massive Entertainment amidst the reorganisation. "Bringing our teams together under one identity gives us the opportunity to combine the creative energy and expertise across Montréal, Paris, Sweden and Toronto to shape the next generation of these iconic franchises, create new games and IPs, and push our craft and technology forward," he said.
Nothing further was revealed about March of Giants, other than its name, and that it's an original game idea.

articles.summary: On Oct. 1, Netflix Anime announced that Dragon Ball Super: Beerus, the upcoming remake of the Dragon Ball Super anime, will be available on the popular streaming platform. A release date has not been specified, with the announcement only stating that the anime is coming in October.

Anime streaming platform Crunchyroll, which broadcast the original Dragon Ball Super anime, has not yet made any official announcements regarding the remake. Meanwhile, we now know the anime will be available internationally on Netflix in some regions, but we don't know the exact release date.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus will offer a modern retelling of the first three arcs of the Dragon Ball Super anime (and of the franchise's first two movies). It's a direct sequel to Dragon Ball Z, taking place four years after the defeat of Majin Buu, during the 10-year time skip shown in the final episode of the original series. Goku and his friends have to face a whole new level of threats, starting with the mighty God of Destruction, Beerus. Of course, this means more training and power-ups are on the way, too.

articles.title: "Extraction is Still a Major Part of Marathon" – Marathon Game Director Reassures Fans Main Game Mode Isn't Going Anywhere
articles.summary: Just last week, Marathon's developers laid out a new roadmap for the game that'd bring PvE and deathmatch modes to the game, but now Game Director Del Chafe has reassured fans that the extraction mode will not be sunsetted.
body: When Bungie revealed the roadmap last week, some people were worried that the more hardcore extraction mode would be neglected in favor of the new modes, especially after the developer admitted that Marathon flopped because it was too hard. But, using the Marathon Development Team Twitter account, Chafe reassured folks, saying "We want to be clear, Extraction is still a major part of Marathon, and we're also going to continue updating it as we look to the future of the game."

Chafe also asked fans for feedback, saying "We'd love to hear from you on what you're enjoying about Extraction today, what you think needs work, and what you wish was there." Of course, Marathon fans obliged.

Marathon streamer Drewsky replied, saying that the among the main problems facing the extraction mode are spawn rushes and harsh death spirals that price players out. User nsorrey36 echoed Drewsky, saying "Echoing a lot of sentiment where it feels like lobby wiping is the go-to strategy of the run."

articles.title: AMD's new 'Gainsborough' APU rumoured to be the chip that powers the long-awaited Steam Deck 2
articles.summary: The original Steam Deck went on sale about four and a half years ago. And there hasn't been any clear indication that a true second-gen handheld from Valve is imminent. Until now, that is.
body: YouTube channel Moore's Law is Dead has a new video explaining how a rumoured AMD APU known as Gainsborough is likely to be the chip that powers the next-gen Steam Deck 2 handheld.

The MLID channel is admittedly not everyone's cup of tea, but has had some notable hits over the years when it comes to leaks and rumours. With that caveat covered off, what do we know about Gainsborough?
First, the codename does actually make sense. The OG Deck's APU was known as Aerith, as in the character from Final Fantasy 7. And Aerith's second same is, of course, Gainsborough.

In terms of the technicalities, there isn't a huge amount of information. However, one critical tidbit is that it will be built on TSMC's N3P node. That's TSMC's fanciest, most advanced and most efficient version of its N3 family of chip production nodes. That matters because it should make for a more efficient chip for a handheld where battery life is critical.

articles.title: 60 Years After Her Peanuts Debut, Peppermint Patty Is Still the Best Friend Charlie Brown Ever Had
articles.summary: If you're at all interested in Charles Schulz's Peanuts, it's a good idea to invest in Fantagraphics' The Complete Peanuts. It's a 26-volume set that contains every strip that saw publication, with around two years of strips per book.
body: Reading through Peanuts as a single unbroken run is a unique experience for anyone who's a fan of the strip or the medium. You get to watch the characters and art evolve day by day, from the early gags featuring now-little-known characters like Violet to the slow appearance of what becomes the established crew. It's also a useful way to start developing strong opinions about all these 75-year-old comic strip characters, like how Peppermint Patty doesn't get nearly enough credit for being the best friend Charlie Brown ever had.

Friendship in Peanuts is one of its more incidental themes. As with a number of other subjects, the strip itself doesn't often have that much to explicitly say on the topic, but there's official merchandise that does. For example, there are at least two Peanuts collections based around it, such as 2016's The Peanuts Guide to Friendship. The strip itself never makes a concrete statement about it... unless, arguably, Peppermint Patty is involved.

articles.title: I spent far too long assigning gaming mouse values based on their price-to-weight ratio, and the runner-up is the rodent on my desk right now
articles.summary: James is a more recent PC gaming convert, often admiring graphics cards, cases, and motherboards from afar. It was not until 2019, after just finishing a degree in law and media, that they decided to throw out the last few years of education, build their PC, and start writing about gaming…
body: You may know the trick of checking price in relation to weight, rather than full price, at a supermarket, to account for different pack sizes, but have you ever thought of applying that same metric to gaming mice? Me neither, until our Dave spotted such a rubric on Amazon. The Turtle Beach Burst II Air Amazon listing has a price-to-ounce ratio, and that got me thinking: which mouse would offer the best price-to-gram ratio?

Yes, it may be a bit silly to value price relative to weight, as it's favouring cheap but heavy mice, and it might mean that some ultralight mice get the short end of the stick, and some might argue that price-to-gram tells you less about whether you should buy the mouse than price by itself, but you've gotta take that one up with Mr Bezos. I'm just the messenger, and as we all know, the messenger never gets shot.

As a fierce rodent scientist, I fear this specific study needs much more than just working out the weight-to-price ratio. Thus, my own personal rubric was born, an unholy alliance of two different scores that are then averaged together.

articles.title: Nvidia says my RTX 4070 Super isn't capable of Multi Frame Gen, but I'm surprised by how smooth this unofficial unlock actually feels
articles.summary: Jess has been writing about games for over ten years, spending a significant chunk of that time working on print publications PLAY and Official PlayStation Magazine.
body: Multi Frame Generation (or MFG) smoothes out gameplay by using AI to create as many as five generated, or 'fake' frames for each one actually rendered by the GPU. Nvidia first introduced the original 2x Frame Generation feature with the RTX 40-series graphics cards back in 2022, but the highest rates of frame gen are reserved for the RTX 50-series.

If you have an RTX 5090 (despite it being particularly tricky to find one, let alone for a price anywhere near MSRP ), you can enjoy as much as 6x MFG in supported games. This is because the RTX 50-series GPUs contain more powerful Tensor cores, but also a dedicated AI Management Processor (AMP) which works alongside Flip Metering to deliver frames, both rendered and AI-generated, to your display as smoothly as possible. Older cards, like my RTX 4070 Super, lack this snazzy silicon—but us PC gamers won't let something as silly as official limitations stop us.

articles.title: Resident Evil Requiem Producer “Explains” Game’s Title, Confusing Us More
articles.summary: The meaning of Resident Evil Requiem's title appeared to be self-evident when it was released earlier this year. However, Resident Evil producer Jun Takeuchi's explanation for the title from the recently published Biohazard 30th Anniversary Special may be a head-scratcher for even the series'…
body: "'Requiem' isn't just a title chosen for its meaning of 'requiem,'" said Takeuchi via GamesRadar. "The spelling of Requiem (REQUIEM) contains not only the 'RE (response)'... but also a 'Q (question).' In other words, this 'Requiem' presents both an 'answer' and a 'question.' I will explain the meaning of that at some point in the future."
More intriguingly, Takeuchi indicated that the Resident Evil remake games and the current titles have been building towards a crossover since Resident Evil Village.

"Currently, Resident Evil operates on a two-pronged approach: The numbered titles allow players to experience the ongoing drama of the series, while the remake series lets them experience the past," added Takeuchi. "Eventually, the remake series will catch up to the era of the numbered titles, and the mechanisms for that are already being considered. In fact, preparations for this have been gradually underway since Resident Evil Village, including the appearance of names like Umbrella and Spencer, and the reappearance of Raccoon City in Requiem. This is all in preparation for a crossover."
